message.content: Existing fusion research has already benefited society in practical ways. Plasma diagnostics developed for fusion help improve medical imaging and materials testing. Superconducting magnet research supports MRI scanners and power grid components. High vacuum technology and neutron shielding expertise are reused in semiconductor and nuclear waste facilities. iritic studies have also trained engineers who now advance industrial and climate technologies. These efforts create jobs, safety standards, and pathways toward reliable clean energy. Together, these examples show that fusion science produces transferable tools and economic value before final power plants today.
